profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer @ Bloomberg | LLM agent systems & MCP tooling · Python backend (FastAPI, asyncio, Celery) · Telemetry frameworks & developer tooling
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
I build LLM agent systems and the Python backend and telemetry infrastructure underneath them.

At Bloomberg I started a self-initiated LLM agent prototype that uses MCP tools to investigate engineering tickets across ticketing, code search and documentation. After I presented it at Bloomberg's engineering Guild Week in London, it led to an internal multi-agent LLM system that I co-built and remain a core contributor to. On that system I built the ticket-routing and investigation pipeline behind an async FastAPI service with SSE streaming, added per-ticket concurrency control so the same ticket can't trigger duplicate LLM runs, and built an agent-to-agent integration with timeouts, cancellation and heartbeats, with OpenTelemetry trace propagation.

On the platform side, I designed and shipped a self-telemetry framework for a distributed Python/Celery service. A single wrapper at the dispatch seam instruments every task type without touching task code, and a drift test keeps the dashboards-as-code in sync with the metrics. Rolling it out also surfaced and closed a coverage gap in the existing telemetry. I also added a CI guard that turns silent metric loss into a build failure.

Before Bloomberg I spent six years at Intel on developer infrastructure: a Perforce-to-GitHub migration, a cross-platform GitHub webhook service, a per-repository resource allocation system, and a Python scheduler for remote hardware testing.

BS Computer Engineering, UIUC.

I'm looking for senior software engineering roles on AI agent platforms, LLM developer tooling, and backend or developer platforms.

positions.description:
I build Python backend services, telemetry frameworks and LLM agent tooling for Bloomberg's index-calculation platform. 

• Started an LLM agent for engineering ticket investigation as a self-initiated prototype, using MCP tools for ticketing, code search and documentation, with guardrails for accuracy, security and verification. Engineers outside my team have since contributed their own configurations. After I presented it at Bloomberg's engineering Guild Week in London, it led to an internal multi-agent LLM system, co-built with another engineer, where I'm a core contributor. 

• On that system, built the routing and investigation pipeline behind an async FastAPI service with SSE streaming, added per-ticket concurrency control to prevent duplicate LLM runs, and built an agent-to-agent integration (timeouts, cancellation, heartbeats) with OpenTelemetry trace propagation. 

• Designed and shipped a self-telemetry framework for a distributed Python/Celery service. One wrapper at the dispatch seam instruments every task type with no task-code changes, and a drift test keeps the dashboards-as-code in sync with the metrics. The rollout also surfaced and closed a coverage gap in the existing telemetry. 

• Built a pytest-based deployment verification package with separate gating and shadow suites, designed against false greens.
positions.insights: Large Language Models (LLM), AI Agents and +3 skills

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Developer infrastructure and internal tooling for Intel's Programmable Solutions Group (PSG). Progressed from Software Engineer to Senior Software Engineer. 

• Selected as a core engineer on the move of code integration and deployment from a Perforce monorepo to distributed GitHub repositories. Co-designed and validated a repository-segmentation proof of concept aimed at faster, more scalable deployments. 

• Built a cross-platform (Linux/Windows) Python webhook service that connects GitHub workflow events to proprietary execution environments. 

• Led development of a per-repository resource allocation system: teams declare memory, CPU and executor requirements, and the system allocates them dynamically. 

• Designed and built an in-house Python scheduling system for running tests remotely on hardware boards (DUTs). 

• Reverse-engineered a legacy Perl tool to extract its requirements and address the pain points in its design. 

• Developed features for internal developer code-testing tools.

positions.description:
• Reverse-engineered and extended Python pipeline scripts that feed data from multiple monitors into an intrusion-detection system. 
• Added Kafka message queuing to the pipeline to prevent event loss.
